articles.title: From sketch to final touch
articles.excerpt: A painting does not arrive all at once. This portrait sequence shows the patience behind the work: paper sketch, canvas draft, color layers, refinement, and final detail.

sections.heading: The first line is a thinking space
sections.body: The paper sketch is where proportion, pose, and feeling are tested without pressure. It lets the artist understand the subject before committing to the canvas.

sections.heading: The canvas starts rough on purpose
sections.body: The next stage is not meant to look finished. A loose canvas draft gives the piece structure, checks the placement, and leaves room for correction before color takes over.

sections.heading: Color builds the emotion
sections.body: The first painted layer sets the mood, then later passes deepen the fabric, face, light, and surrounding details. Each layer makes the work more confident without losing the softness of the original idea.

sections.heading: The final touch shows patience
sections.body: The finished piece carries evidence of all the earlier decisions. That sequence says a lot about the artist: she observes carefully, changes direction when needed, and gives the work time to become complete.

articles.title: Behind the making table
articles.excerpt: A look at how references, color, material, and occasion come together before a handmade piece begins.

sections.heading: Start with the moment
sections.body: The strongest pieces begin with the person and the occasion. A few references, colors, and practical details help shape the right direction.

sections.heading: Then shape the material
sections.body: Each medium behaves differently. Texture work needs depth, outline work needs clean balance, and decor work needs structure, finish, and presentation.

articles.title: How to care for handmade pieces
articles.excerpt: Simple care habits for storing, gifting, and displaying handcrafted decor, textile detail, and keepsakes.

sections.heading: Keep it dry and supported
sections.body: Store delicate pieces away from moisture and pressure. Use a flat surface or protective box for decor and keepsakes.

sections.heading: Handle details gently
sections.body: Small decorative elements can be strong but still need careful handling, especially during gifting, packing, or event setup.

sections.heading: Make presentation part of the piece
